LESSON: GRAMMAR IN USE 11.3.1 FORMATION OF ADJECTIVES

Grade: Grade 7
Subject: ENGLISH
Strand: Strand 11
Topic 11.3: Grammar in Use 11.3.1 Formation of Adjectives

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Grammar in Use 11.3.1 Formation of Adjectives. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: How are adjectives formed?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. recognise adjectives from a text
2. construct simple sentences using the adjectives formed
3. appreciate the value of proper use of adjectives

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: GRAMMAR IN USE 11.3.1 FORMATION OF ADJECTIVES
Subject: ENGLISH · Grade: Grade 7
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Grammar in Use 11.3.1 Formation of Adjectives helps you succeed in ENGLISH. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

KEY FACTS: GRAMMAR IN USE 11.3.1 FORMATION OF ADJECTIVES
Language skills grow by daily practice: listen carefully, speak clearly, read every day, write neatly.
Model → guided practice → independent practice.
Always use complete sentences when writing answers.

PART 1: Recognise adjectives from a text

What this means
In this part you learn to recognise adjectives from a text. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: recognise adjectives from a text.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model reading: Read a short paragraph about “Grammar in Use 11.3.1 Formation of Adjectives”, then retell it in 3 sentences.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can recognise adjectives from a text. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Construct simple sentences using the adjectives formed

What this means
In this part you learn to construct simple sentences using the adjectives formed. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: construct simple sentences using the adjectives formed.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model speaking: Say 4 clear sentences about Grammar in Use 11.3.1 Formation of Adjectives to a partner.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can construct simple sentences using the adjectives formed. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 3: Appreciate the value of proper use of adjectives

What this means
In this part you learn to appreciate the value of proper use of adjectives. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: appreciate the value of proper use of adjectives.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model writing: Write 5 neat sentences using new words from this lesson.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can appreciate the value of proper use of adjectives. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Grammar in Use 11.3.1 Formation of Adjectives is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Read a short paragraph about “Grammar in Use 11.3.1 Formation of Adjectives”, then retell it in 3 sentences. (skill: recognise adjectives from a text)

Example 2: Say 4 clear sentences about Grammar in Use 11.3.1 Formation of Adjectives to a partner. (skill: construct simple sentences using the adjectives formed)

Example 3: Write 5 neat sentences using new words from this lesson. (skill: appreciate the value of proper use of adjectives)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Grammar in Use 11.3.1 Formation of Adjectives to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: recognise adjectives from a text.
3. Practise this skill: construct simple sentences using the adjectives formed.
4. Practise this skill: appreciate the value of proper use of adjectives.
5. Make one local Kenya example of Grammar in Use 11.3.1 Formation of Adjectives from your county, market, farm, or school.
6. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Grammar in Use 11.3.1 Formation of Adjectives: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 7 learner study Grammar in Use 11.3.1 Formation of Adjectives?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. How are adjectives formed?
2. Why should we use adjectives correctly?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Grammar in Use 11.3.1 Formation of Adjectives means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: recognise adjectives from a text.
5. Be able to: construct simple sentences using the adjectives formed.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
